description: The member cap a submission set is admitted under, and the system-wide constants every artifact carries. Fixes the values two implementations must agree on before a single byte is hashed.
why_this_is_a_primitive: These are not digests, so nothing here recomputes. They are the numbers and strings that decide ADMISSION: a producer that caps at one value and a consumer that caps at another disagree about whether a set is well-formed, and the disagreement surfaces as a rejection nobody can reproduce. Pinning them makes the boundary a contract rather than a constant each implementation happens to carry.

member_cap.rule: A submission set carries at least 1 and at most 64 members. The bound is inclusive: exactly 64 is admissible, 65 is not.
member_cap.source: submission-set/1 §8.1: MAX_SUBMISSION_SET_MEMBERS = 64, a fixed protocol constant. A member carries a capacity.evidence/1 and never subject content, so its size does not grow with subject count or collection cardinality, and the member cap bounds the set directly (submission-set/1 §8.1).
member_cap.note_for_implementers: The cap must be enforced where the set is ASSEMBLED, not only where it is submitted. A producer that builds an over-sized set and discovers the cap at the transport layer has already spent the operation key leaves it grouped.

cardinality_cases.name: single member
cardinality_cases.why: the minimum viable set; a set of one is the common case for a low-volume issuer

cardinality_cases.name: at the cap
cardinality_cases.why: the bound is inclusive — an implementation using < instead of <= rejects a set every other implementation accepts

cardinality_cases.name: one over the cap
cardinality_cases.why: the first inadmissible count; this is the case that catches an off-by-one in either direction

cardinality_cases.name: empty set
cardinality_cases.why: a set with no members has no submission to close over. Its submission_set_id would still compute, so nothing downstream catches it — the emptiness must be refused where the set is built

cardinality_cases.name: far over the cap
cardinality_cases.why: well beyond the cap. An over-cardinality set is malformed at the set level, so it is refused as a whole, before any per-member evaluation and before any capacity is consumed (submission-set/1 §8.1)

system_id.rule: The active system identity every artifact carries, in the `system_id` field. It is part of the signed bytes of capacity.evidence/1, operator.receipt/1, capacity.holder-authorization/1 and the settlement leaf preimage.
system_id.why_pinned: It sits inside signed preimages, so a divergent value is not a mislabel — it is a different digest. An implementation that defaults it, or derives it per environment, signs bytes no other implementation reproduces.

signature_algorithm.rule: The active signature-algorithm tag carried alongside a signature value.

composite_profile.rule: The composite signature profile: ECDSA P-256 AND ML-DSA-65, both required. The profile id is framed into M′ before signing, so it is part of what is signed and not merely a label.

system_constant_cases.name: system_id case variation rejected
system_constant_cases.why: the comparison is byte-exact, not case-folded — these are different bytes in a signed preimage

system_constant_cases.name: system_id with surrounding space rejected
system_constant_cases.why: no trimming: an implementation that trims before comparing accepts bytes it would not itself produce

must_hold: a set of exactly 64 members is admitted, and 65 is not
an empty set is refused where the set is assembled, not at the transport layer
system_id, the signature-algorithm tag and the composite profile id are compared byte-exactly — no case folding, no trimming, no default
these constants appear inside signed preimages, so a divergent value changes the digest rather than only the label
